Optional boss
Had the patient's pyrexia been attributable to a bacterial aetiology, one would have anticipated a neutrophilic leucocytosis rather than the leucopenia and thrombocytopenia observed, which, in conjunction with the exanthem, are more consistent with an arboviral infection; antibiotics were therefore withheld.
Why did the doctor NOT give antibiotics?
90
🔒
Free pass
Stuck? Tap 😵‍💫 when your team is ready.
Free pass
pyrexia = fever
bacterial = from bacteria
leucopenia = low white cells
thrombocytopenia = low platelets
exanthem = rash
arboviral = a virus from insects (mosquitoes)
The fever was not from bacteria. Her white cells and platelets were LOW, and she had a rash. That fits a virus carried by mosquitoes (dengue).
Because dengue is a virus. Antibiotics work on bacteria, not on viruses.
